'''Yuriy Reznikov''' (16 October 1953 – 8 October 2016) was a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[physicist]], Head of the Department of Crystals at [[NASU Institute of Physics]] and a world-renown expert in the field of [[liquid crystal]]s. He is known for his work on [[photoalignment]], "giant" optical non-linearity of liquid crystals and nano-colloids.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reznikov|first1=M.|last2=Andrienko|first2=D.|last3=Boychuk|first3=V. N.|last4=Bubnov|first4=A.|last5=Dolgov|first5=L.|last6=Dozov|first6=I.|last7=Davidson|first7=P.|last8=Gabovich|first8=A.|last9=Hegmann|first9=T.|last10=Ilchishin|first10=I.|last11=Karapinar|first11=R.|date=2018-10-01|title=Recollections of Professor Yuriy Reznikov|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732218343642|journal=Journal of Molecular Liquids|series=Special Issue Dedicated to the Memory of Professor Y. Reznikov|language=en|volume=267|pages=11–28|doi=10.1016/j.molliq.2018.08.127|s2cid=105826354 |issn=0167-7322|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Yuriy Reznikov received his Master's degree in [[radiophysics]] from [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]] in 1976. In 1985, he received his [[doctorate]] in physics in [[NASU Institute of Physics]]. His Ph.D. thesis was titled “The study of the optical nonlinearity of liquid crystals near their electron absorption bands”. In 1995, Yuriy has received his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree after defending the thesis titled “Light Induced Impurities in Liquid Crystals”. Since 1995, he was a head of the [http://lcnet.org.ua/ Department of Crystals] in [[NASU Institute of Physics]].

== Research ==
During 1979-1984 Yuriy Reznikov has discovered and studied “Giant” optical nonlinearity of [[liquid crystal]]s caused by [[Phototransformation|photo-transformation]] of their molecules (so called “conformational nonlinearity”).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Simoni|first1=F.|last2=Lucchetti|first2=L.|date=2018-10-01|title=Colossal nonlinear optical response of liquid crystals|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732217351127|journal=Journal of Molecular Liquids|series=Special Issue Dedicated to the Memory of Professor Y. Reznikov|language=en|volume=267|pages=67–72|doi=10.1016/j.molliq.2017.12.121|hdl=11566/255664 |s2cid=104051434 |issn=0167-7322|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Prof. Francesco Simoni of [[Polytechnic University of the Marches]] ([[Ancona]], Italy) wrote in his condolence for the death of Yuriy: “This nonlinearity is considered as a milestone for researches that followed and had many consequences as the ones related to effects of photo-isomerization on the liquid crystalline state carried out by several groups over the world and leading to the exciting research of photomobile materials”. The conformational nonlinearity then was applied for optical information processing and hologram recording.

After finishing the PhD thesis Yuriy has developed a method to measure the [[liquid crystal]] anchoring energy using [[Scattering|light scattering]] technique.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Marusii|first=T.Ya.|date=September 1986|title=Scattering of light by nematic liquid crystals in cells with a finite energy of the anchoring of the director to the wails|url=http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/e/index/e/64/3/p502?a=list|journal=[[Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics]]|volume=64|issue=3 |pages=502|bibcode=1986JETP...64..502M }}</ref> In the 1985-89 he has also studied the effect of a light-induced change of a [[Cholesteric liquid crystal|cholesteric]] pitch under molecular [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167732217351127?via%3Dihub photo-transformations].

Later on in 1989-1995 Yuriy’s significant accomplishments include the development of the [[photoalignment]] technology and control of the [[liquid crystal]] anchoring parameters by [[photoalignment]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dyadyusha|first1=A. G.|last2=Marusii|first2=T. Ya.|last3=Reznikov|first3=Yu. A.|last4=Khizhnyak|first4=A. I.|last5=Reshetnyak|first5=V. Yu.|date=1992-07-01|title=Orientational effect due to a change in the anisotropy of the interaction between a liquid crystal and a bounding surface|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1992JETPL..56...17D|journal=Soviet Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics Letters|volume=56|pages=17|bibcode=1992JETPL..56...17D|issn=0021-3640}}</ref> technique. His groundbreaking work has paved the way for the development of this technology all the way to the widespread use in the LCD manufacturing since 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yaroshchuk|first1=Oleg|last2=Reznikov|first2=Yuriy|date=2011-12-08|title=Photoalignment of liquid crystals: basics and current trends|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2012/jm/c1jm13485j|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry|language=en|volume=22|issue=2|pages=286–300|doi=10.1039/C1JM13485J|issn=1364-5501|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Other Yuriy's achievements in this time frame include conformational optical nonlinearity in two-phase region of liquid crystals, surface-driven reorientation effects in [[liquid crystal]] cells with photosensitive aligning layer.

Since 1995, Yuriy’s main milestones include light manipulation of [[nanoparticle]]s in arrays of [[topological defect]]s, developing a technique to measure ultra-large [[Cholesteric liquid crystal|cholesteric]] pitch, studying orientational coupling in two-component suspensions of rod-like nanoparticles, discovering strong thermal optical nonlinearity in liquid crystalline metal [[Colloid|nano-colloids]], developing stable liquid crystal ferromagnetic [[Colloid|nano-colloids]], observation of high magnetic sensitivity of the aggregated [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnetic]] [[Colloid|nano-colloids]], surface mediated photorefraction in liquid crystals, developing rollable bistable plastic [[Liquid-crystal display|liquid crystal displays]], studying diluted liquid crystal [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectric]] nano-colloids, finding surface [[bistability]] in liquid crystals sandwiched between photo-aligning surfaces.
